content: Obesity is a risk factor for the development of several cancers, including breast, colorectal, and gynecologic carcinomas.1,2 More recently, it has become clear that obesity is associated not only with carcinogenesis but also with prognosis in several types of cancer. For example, obesity has been linked to poor prognosis in breast3,4 and colorectal cancers,5,6 whereas favorable outcomes have been reported in obese patients with gastric7 and renal8 cancers.
